 Saturday, October 3, 2026 · 13 games tonight, first puck 7:00 PM ET

Game of the night

Bruins at Wild

8:00 PM ET at Grand Casino Arena

Boston is 2-0 and neither win was boring. Jeremy Swayman shut out the Rangers in the opener, then Friday in Winnipeg the Bruins trailed late until Elias Lindholm tied it with the goalie pulled and JJ Peterka won it 3:21 into overtime.

Power rankings · Preseason

  1. 1

    Carolina Hurricanes

    0-1-1Record0.50PTS/GP-4Goal diff0-1-1Last 10+750Cup odds

    The champs until someone takes it: 113 points, then the Cup in six over Vegas. Andersen left and Jarvis misses about the first 10 games, but Bussi closed out the Final with a shutout.

  2. 2

    Dallas Stars

    0-1-0Record0.00PTS/GP-4Goal diff0-1-0Last 10+1600Cup odds

    112 points, and Jason Robertson (96 points) re-signed, ending the trade chatter. Losing Bourque is a depth hit, not a core one.

  3. 3

    Colorado Avalanche

    1-0-0Record2.00PTS/GP+4Goal diff1-0-0Last 10+750Cup odds

    121 points and a +99 goal differential, both best in the league. Nichushkin and Drury are gone; MacKinnon and Makar (back in full practice) keep them a coin flip with Carolina for the top spot.

  4. 4

    Florida Panthers

    1-0-1Record1.50PTS/GP+0Goal diff1-0-1Last 10+750Cup odds

    84 points last season came without Barkov, who missed the whole year after knee surgery. He's back, Brady Tkachuk and Markstrom arrived, and the market has them as Cup favorites. Marchand misses the start.

  5. 5

    Montreal Canadiens

    1-0-0Record2.00PTS/GP+1Goal diff1-0-0Last 10+2200Cup odds

    106 points and still climbing, and now Chris Kreider is skating on the top line with Suzuki and Caufield. Guhle misses the first four to five weeks.

  6. 6

    Tampa Bay Lightning

    0-1-0Record0.00PTS/GP-4Goal diff0-1-0Last 10+1200Cup odds

    106 points and +59. Gourde (hip) is out until December and Paul and Raddysh left; John Carlson on the blue line softens the blow.

  7. 7

    Vegas Golden Knights

    1-1-0Record1.00PTS/GP+2Goal diff1-1-0Last 10+1100Cup odds

    Cup finalists, but Pietrangelo is on LTIR for the whole season and Dorofeyev was traded to the Rangers. New coach Ryan Craig takes over a team the market still rates highly.

  8. 8

    Minnesota Wild

    1-0-0Record2.00PTS/GP+2Goal diff1-0-0Last 10+1300Cup odds

    104 points and +32. Gustavsson is out until about November after hip surgery, and Zuccarello and Tarasenko are gone, with Blake Coleman in to help.

  9. 9

    Edmonton Oilers

    1-0-1Record1.50PTS/GP+1Goal diff1-0-1Last 10+1000Cup odds

    McDavid and Draisaitl under Mike Babcock, but Andersen got hurt in training, so it may be Devon Levi's net early. Until the goaltending settles, this is a top-10 team, not a top-5 one.

  10. 10

    Buffalo Sabres

    0-1-0Record0.00PTS/GP-3Goal diff0-1-0Last 10+3300Cup odds

  11. 11

    1-0-0Record2.00PTS/GP+6Goal diff1-0-0Last 10+2700Cup odds

Saturday, October 3

Game recap

NYR2DET0Final: NYR 2, DET 0

Detroit's home opener had everything a long-suffering fan base could want: booing their own former captain before puck drop, then 60 minutes of not scoring. Dylan Garand, the Rangers' fill-in on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped all 22 shots for the shutout, which is what happens when the other team's shots arrive gift-wrapped. Sean Durzi scored on the power play 5:12 in and later fought Marco Kasper, a full night's work before the third period. Eeli Tolvanen hit the empty net with 1:16 left. John Gibson made 19 saves on 20 and got nothing for it but a sympathetic slap on the pads. New York is 2-1 and has won two straight. Detroit is 0-1, has no goals, no captain and a 10-season playoff drought, and the season is one game old.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

WSH5CAR2Final: WSH 5, CAR 2

The Capitals walked into the champs' building and had it 3-0 before the first intermission, the hockey version of showing up to a party and eating the cake. Alex Tuch scored twice in his Washington debut, and rookie defenseman Cole Hutson scored in his NHL debut, which beats the usual first-game souvenir of a puck and a nervous smile. Ovechkin got an assist on the opening goal, Jakob Chychrun had a power-play goal and an assist, and Dylan Strome and Pierre-Luc Dubois had two helpers each. Sebastian Aho finally got Carolina a power-play goal in the second, and Ryan Leonard answered eight seconds later, which is just rude. Logan Thompson made 31 saves on 33; Brandon Bussi let in five on 27. The Hurricanes outshot Washington and lost by three: 0-1-1, one goal in two home games, and the banner is already the best thing they've put up this season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

BOS4WPG3OTFinal: BOS 4, WPG 3 OT

Winnipeg's home opener was a lovely evening right up until the last 1:38. The Jets led 3-2 after Mario Ferraro scored with eight seconds left in the second, Kyle Connor had a power-play goal, an assist and nine shots, and the Canada Life Centre was ready to go home happy. Then Boston pulled Jeremy Swayman, and Elias Lindholm tied it 6-on-5 at 18:22 of the third. JJ Peterka, two games into his Bruins career, won it 3:21 into overtime for his second goal. David Pastrnak and Nikita Zadorov set up two goals each, Hampus Lindholm and James Hagens also scored, and Mark Kastelic and Tyrel Bauer dropped the gloves early. Swayman stopped 30 of 33, Stuart Skinner 26 of 30. Boston is 2-0. Winnipeg got a point for its trouble, and a reminder that its former Vezina winner is still suspended for skipping camp and still waiting on a trade. Nothing says 'new season' like the old goalie problem.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

STL4DAL0Final: STL 4, DAL 0

Dallas spent the summer near the top of everybody's rankings and opened its season by getting shut out at home. Mason McTavish, playing his first game as a Blue, scored 94 seconds in, and the Stars spent the next 58 minutes looking for a reply. Dalibor Dvorsky made it 2-0 in the second, then St. Louis hit the empty net twice in 15 seconds, Jimmy Snuggerud and Pius Suter, with Joel Hofer picking up an assist on the second one. Hofer stopped all 25 shots for the shutout and outscored the entire Dallas roster in points. Jake Oettinger made 20 saves on 22 and deserved a better band in front of him. Jake Neighbours and Arttu Hyry fought in the second, the closest Dallas came to winning a battle all night. A 112-point team with Jason Robertson locked up, and the first goal of their season will have to wait for Nashville.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

ANA4VGK3Final: ANA 4, VGK 3

Anaheim's season opener in Vegas went great for about 45 minutes and then got very Vegas. Beckett Sennecke scored with eight seconds left in the first, Alex Killorn and Jeff Malott scored 55 seconds apart early in the second, and Leo Carlsson, the guy the Ducks paid to keep away from Philadelphia, made it 4-0 at 7:03. The Golden Knights trailed by four on home ice to a team that just lost half its summer roster, and the Strip briefly considered a dinner show. Then Shea Theodore, Tomas Hertl on the power play and Braeden Bowman with 2:50 left made it 4-3, and Jack Eichel had two assists in the rally. Lukas Dostal held on with 27 saves on 30. Carter Hart let in four on 20. Vegas played the last 20 minutes like Cup finalists and the first 40 like the house was comping the other team.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Friday, October 2

Game recap

PHI2NJD3OTFinal: PHI 2, NJD 3 OT

The Devils threw 44 shots at Joseph Woll, the hockey version of trying every key on the ring. Woll stopped 41 and dragged Philly to overtime, where Jack Hughes ended it at 3:23, because of course he did. The Flyers led twice: once on a Rasmus Ristolainen goal with their own goalie on the bench (bold), once on Travis Sanheim's goal early in the third. Both leads lasted about as long as a Philly sports-radio caller's patience. Dougie Hamilton and Luke Hughes did the tying, Bratt set up the winner, and Jake Allen needed only 23 saves. Tocchet shortened his bench so much that Porter Martone watched most of the third from the best seat in the house. One point and a minus-8 goal difference after two games: the Flyers are rebuilding, and so far the foundation is Joseph Woll and a lot of prayer.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

TBL1NYR5Final: TBL 1, NYR 5

Igor Shesterkin stopped 24 of 25 and then, apparently tired of waiting on his forwards, scored into the empty net himself. A goalie goal in the home opener: the Garden hasn't been this giddy since the last time somebody promised a parade. Zibanejad scored on the power play and set up another, Dorofeyev had two points, and Adam Fox handed out two assists like party favors. Tolvanen and Gabe Perreault joined in. Kucherov got one back in the second and then spent the night watching. Andrei Vasilevskiy let in four on 24 shots, not the opening act Tampa sold tickets for. Final tally: the entire Lightning roster scored one goal, exactly as many as the guy in the Rangers' crease, and he was busy making 24 saves at the time.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

BUF3CBJ6Final: BUF 3, CBJ 6

Matthew Knies' first game in a Blue Jackets sweater: two goals, an assist and, presumably, a thank-you card in the mail to Columbus. Charlie Coyle had three assists, Werenski two, and Columbus scored six on 23 shots, efficiency Buffalo can only read about. The Sabres hung around, 4-3 after two thanks to Quinn and Helenius, then remembered who they were. Luukkonen stopped 17 of 22, a save percentage best described as 'hospitable'. Mathieu Olivier fought Zach Metsa and then scored into the empty net, a full shift's work in one night. Owen Power and Noah Ostlund had two assists each, nice consolation prizes. Buffalo opened the season with 'this is the year' energy and closed the first night with 'here we go again.'

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

MIN3NSH1Final: MIN 3, NSH 1

Nashville rolled out the home-opener pageantry and the Wild treated it like a soundcheck. Nick Foligno opened the scoring, Blake Coleman added a power-play goal, and Kaprizov put it away early in the third off a Quinn Hughes feed, a sentence Wild fans waited all summer to say. Hughes played 27:30 and looked like he'd been there for years. Jesper Wallstedt needed 19 saves, a light shift. Josi scored, Stamkos and Forsberg got assists, and the Preds managed 20 shots in their own building, roughly one per sad country song. Saros made 27 saves and deserved a better band behind him. Nashville spent big two summers ago to win now, and 'now' keeps showing up looking like this.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

SEA6CGY1Final: SEA 6, CGY 1

Calgary's home opener was over about 19 and a half minutes in, when the Kraken went up 3-0 and the Saddledome started checking the parking-lot traffic. Vince Dunn had three points, Jared McCann three assists, and Joey Daccord stopped 24 of 25 and still found time for an assist, which is one more point than the Flames' entire defense managed. Seattle's scoresheet read like a roll call: Eberle, Dunn, Gaudreau, Stephenson, Beniers, Kakko. Dustin Wolf faced 32 shots and six went in, and very little of it was his idea. Ryan Strome broke the shutout with 3:25 left, which in Calgary currently counts as a rally. The Flames have a shiny new arena on the way, and on this evidence it'll open before their second goal of the night would have.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

FLA3SJS4OTFinal: FLA 3, SJS 4 OT

The Sharks led Florida 3-0, which in San Jose is screenshot material. Will Smith scored shorthanded and on the power play in the same period, Celebrini set up three goals and put seven shots on net, and the building was ready to name a freeway after somebody. Then the Panthers woke up: Luostarinen twice and Matthew Tkachuk 17 seconds later, because Florida treats a three-goal hole like a mild inconvenience. Luca Cagnoni ended it in overtime anyway. Brady Tkachuk and Jacob Trouba dropped the gloves in the first, and Collin Graf and Uvis Balinskis followed suit in the second, so nobody left without a souvenir. Florida has Cup rings in the trophy case and just lost an overtime to a team that finished dead last in 2025: the champs' swagger made the trip, the finishing touch stayed in Sunrise.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

CHI0UTA6Final: CHI 0, UTA 6

Utah's home opener was a 6-0 party, and the Blackhawks brought 15 shots to it, which isn't a gift so much as an IOU. Dylan Guenther scored twice on the power play, Keller had two assists, and six different Mammoth scored, including Anders Lee in his first home game for his new team. Karel Vejmelka made 15 saves for the shutout and probably had time to reorganize the bench. Arvid Soderblom got a surprise start and 32 shots for his trouble. Ryan Donato fought MacKenzie Weegar in the third, the most competitive thing Chicago did all night. Two games, 0-2, minus-9: Chicago keeps saying the rebuild is almost finished, and the contractor still can't find the net.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

EDM9VAN7Final: EDM 9, VAN 7

Sixteen goals in Vancouver, which is what happens when two teams agree defense is a rumor. McDavid had five points, Draisaitl three, and the Oilers scored twice shorthanded in 34 seconds, which is just rude. It was 8-2 midway through the second and Kevin Lankinen's night was over. Then Edmonton did the most Oilers thing possible and let Vancouver score four straight, Marco Rossi twice, before Draisaitl calmed everybody down on the power play. Devon Levi gave up seven on 22 shots and still got the win, the hockey version of failing the exam and getting into the school anyway. Elias Pettersson had three points and eight hits, so at least one Canuck showed up angry. Vancouver had all summer to figure out how to stop McDavid, and the answer is still a shrug and a goalie change.

canucksarmy.com

Thursday, October 1

Game recap

PIT7PHI0Final: PIT 7, PHI 0

The Flyers had all summer to plan their home opener and still forgot to show up for it. Pittsburgh, a team that's supposedly too old to climb stairs, led 5-0 halfway through the second and kept going. Nick Robertson scored twice, once shorthanded, because even down a man the Pens looked like they had the extra skater. Filip Hallander turned a promotion to the third line into three points. Evgeni Malkin, 40, scored on the power play like it was 2009. Arturs Silovs needed 19 saves for the shutout, which is barely a warmup. Dan Vladar saw 38 shots and seven goals, and that's less on him than on the five guys in front of him who spent the night sightseeing. Philly's last Cup was 1975, and on this evidence nobody in orange is in a hurry to update the banner.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

NYI1TOR2Final: NYI 1, TOR 2

The Leafs won a hockey game, which in Toronto is basically a parade-route announcement. Two first-period goals from the bottom of the lineup, Colton Sissons and Easton Cowan, then 40 minutes of everyone in blue clutching the lead like a coupon. Auston Matthews and William Nylander combined for zero points and two shots, and somehow that's the formula. Anthony Stolarz stopped 26 of 27 on the back half of a back-to-back. The Islanders' only goal came from Emil Heineman while they were a man down, so maybe try that more often. Pete DeBoer's first night on the Island: 27 shots, one goal, and Matthew Schaefer playing 27:45 because apparently nobody else was cleared to. Long Island waited all summer for its team, and the offense is still stuck in traffic on the LIE.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

LAK4COL8Final: LAK 4, COL 8

The Kings found out the hard way that killing penalties isn't optional in Denver. Colorado scored four times on the power play, and LA, in a twist nobody asked for, scored twice while shorthanded, so at least somebody on the Kings enjoyed special teams. Nathan MacKinnon scored twice and still found time to fight Brandt Clarke, a full shift's work in one night. Artturi Lehkonen added two power-play goals, Brock Nelson had three points, and Jared Bednar got a contract extension the same day and celebrated with eight goals. Darcy Kuemper stopped 21 of 29, a save percentage you usually find on a beer-league stat sheet. Artemi Panarin pulled LA within two with the net empty, and Colorado answered twice in 3:15. Life after Kopitar starts with eight goals against and a long flight home to think about it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

heavy.com

Wednesday, September 30

Game recap

FLA1CAR0Final: FLA 1, CAR 0

The defending champs opened their title defense with 15 shots in 65 minutes, which is a very Hurricanes way to play: all forecheck, no evidence. Markstrom barely broke a sweat in his first game as a Panther, and the winner came from a defenseman in overtime, of course the first goal of the season between these two took 64 minutes and 55 seconds. Imama and Deslauriers handled the entertainment portion of the evening in the first period. The rest of it played like a tax audit with better lighting.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

MTL3TOR2Final: MTL 3, TOR 2

Nylander scored before most of Scotiabank Arena found its seats, and for about ten minutes the new-look Leafs looked like a whole new team. Then the Canadiens scored three in a row and it looked like the old one. Alexandre Carrier, a defenseman, scored the unassisted winner, Josh Anderson did Josh Anderson things, and Toronto's late push got them within one and no closer. Marchenko's visa arrived just in time for him to find out what October in Toronto feels like. The good news for the Leafs: they get to try again tonight.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

NYR0BOS3Final: NYR 0, BOS 3

For 56 minutes this was a goalie duel. For the last four it was a Bruins highlight reel: Minten, Peterka, then Kastelic into the empty net, three goals in 75 seconds of game time. Swayman pitched a 24-save shutout, and the Rangers' new-look forward group left with a clean sheet of zeroes in the points column. Dorofeyev fired five shots in his debut, which is five more than the Rangers got past Swayman. Shesterkin got zero help,

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

VAN6EDM5Final: VAN 6, EDM 5

Last season's last-place team walked into Edmonton, went up 5-2, gave all of it back, and won anyway. Hockey is a beautiful, stupid sport. Evan Bouchard put up five points, a hat trick included, and still lost, which is about as cruel as opening night gets, besides letting three in the last two. Paul Cotter scored shorthanded to open it and in overtime to end it, bookending the chaos. Jarry got put on skates letting 6 of 23 go in. Same old story, the oily Edmonton net minders continue to be leaking worse than the Oiler's cup hopes in June.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

Game recap

CHI2VGK5Final: CHI 2, VGK 5

Patrick Kane scored in his first game back in a Blackhawks sweater, the United Center crowd would have loved it, except this was in Las Vegas. Thirty-nine seconds later Noah Hanifin restored the two-goal cushion, which is the kind of hospitality Vegas is famous for. Eichel ran the show with three points and the Knights outshot Chicago 36-26 under their new coach. The Hawks hung around for two periods, and hanging around is progress for a team that finished with 72 points last season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score

News

Kuzmenko on leave after his father was killed in a bear attack in Siberia

Andrei Kuzmenko left for Russia after his father, Alexander, a longtime Russian hockey coach, was killed by a bear on a fishing trip. The Penguins gave no timeline for his return, so his availability for the opener is unclear. GM Kyle Dubas said the organization fully supports the family.

nhl.com
DAL
Prospect

Top prospect Emil Hemming among Stars' latest cuts

Former first-rounder Emil Hemming was sent to AHL Texas with Jack Anderson, Arno Tiefensee, Kyle Burroughs and others, bringing camp to 32. Dallas went 4-0 in the preseason, allowing three goals.

sports.yahoo.com
VGK
Prospect

First-round defense prospect Juho Piiparinen sent to OHL London

Vegas had brought Piiparinen back from Finland's Liiga to look at him in camp, then assigned him to the London Knights.

prohockeyrumors.com
ANA
Prospect

Goalie prospect Damian Clara and six others assigned to AHL San Diego

Anaheim sent Clara, Matt Basgall, Coulson Pitre, Ethan Procyszyn, Yegor Sidorov, Konnor Smith and Herman Traff to San Diego, and returned Jayden Kurtz to the USHL. Camp dropped to 38.

nhl.com
WPG
Lineup

Jets retool special teams after ranking 24th on the PP and 21st on the PK

Winnipeg held its first special-teams practice on Sept. 24 with new power-play and penalty-kill setups. Scott Arniel and Josh Morrissey set a top-10 target for both units.

nhl.com
CHI
Lineup

Kane plays once in preseason on top line with Nazar and Kantserov

Patrick Kane (two years, $16M) debuted Sept. 24 at St. Louis, a 1-0 loss, on a line with Frank Nazar and rookie Roman Kantserov, and the line drove play. He sat out the home finale so his home debut comes Oct. 6. The line is expected to stay together for the Sept. 29 opener at Vegas.

Waivers

Senators waive Merilainen; Ersson locked in as backup

Ottawa waived goalie Leevi Merilainen (.860 SV% last season), and Vancouver claimed him the next day. That makes Samuel Ersson, acquired from Toronto, Linus Ullmark's backup. Ullmark is expected to start the opener.

MIN
Waivers

Wild cut to 27; first-rounder Carson Lambos among eight waived

Minnesota waived Lambos, Kiersted, Schmidt, Bankier, Gambrell, Kirkland, Pitlick and Shaw (all cleared) and assigned seven more to AHL Iowa, including Riley Heidt and Hunter Haight.

LAK
Waivers

Kings waive Chromiak, Guttman, Pederson, Pinelli and Hicketts

All five were waived for assignment to AHL Ontario, leaving 29 in camp (17 forwards, 9 defensemen, 3 goalies).

nhl.com

Wednesday, September 23

WPG
Holdout

Hellebuyck still suspended and holding out; GM says door not closed on his return

Connor Hellebuyck remains at home, suspended since mid-September for not reporting to camp over his trade request. GM Kevin Cheveldayoff says the door isn't closed. Seravalli reports Winnipeg is moving slowly in hopes he changes his mind, and Friedman says the trade market has gone quiet. He has four years left after this season at $8.5M with a full no-move clause.

thehockeynews.com
DET
Injury

Carter Bear day-to-day; Chase Stillman still not cleared for contact

McLellan said prospect Carter Bear has an upper-body injury that could keep him out about a week. Chase Stillman is practicing but not yet cleared for contact after an offseason injury.

nhl.com
OTT
Injury

Zub not expected to be ready for the start of the season

Travis Green said Artem Zub, still recovering from a knee injury from April's playoffs, is progressing slowly. Green doesn't see him ready for the opener. That is later than the earlier 1-2 week estimate.

nhl.com
OTT
Injury

Sanderson, Spence held out as precaution; Foegele back skating

Jake Sanderson and Jordan Spence missed action with minor issues, described as precautionary. Warren Foegele skated for the first time but is still out of the lineup. Chabot was a game-time call on Sept. 23 while awaiting the birth of his first child.

nhl.com
NYR
Injury

Adam Sykora out 4-5 months with a lower-body injury

Sykora, who was pushing for a bottom-six spot, fell awkwardly into the boards after a hit in the preseason opener at New Jersey. He is expected to miss four to five months.

nhl.com
UTA
Injury

Maveric Lamoureux will miss time with an arm/shoulder injury

Defenseman Maveric Lamoureux left the Sept. 22 preseason game at Los Angeles after a high hit, with his right arm hanging. Andre Tourigny says he'll miss some time, pending more tests. No timeline yet.

nhl.com
DET
Return

Larkin skates with team for first time; sits out preseason

Larkin returned to full practice on Sept. 23 for the first time since hurting his upper body in off-ice training. He sat out every preseason game, including the finale. His status for the opener is still unclear.

nhl.com
LAK
GoalieReported

Darcy Kuemper's rough outing may hand the starting job to Anton Forsberg

Kuemper allowed five goals on 34 shots in a 6-3 preseason loss to Utah. Forsberg finished last season as the starter, and Laviolette usually gives one goalie most of the starts.

thehockeynews.com
EDM
NewsReported

Hurricanes and Golden Knights also wanted Alex Formenton before he picked Edmonton

Several teams went after Formenton on his return to North America. Reports say he chose the Oilers because of his ties to Evan Bouchard and assistant coach D.J. Smith from Ottawa. He is expected to get a look in a depth role.

prohockeyrumors.com
FLA
Lineup

Sandis Vilmanis earns third-line spot with Lundell and Luostarinen

Paul Maurice called the 22-year-old a top-nine player and has him on the third line. He had a strong camp after signing a two-year extension in July.

nhl.com
PHI
Lineup

Tocchet rebuilds the power play around a young top unit

After finishing last in the league on the power play (15.7%), the Flyers' new PP1 is Zegras, Martone, Michkov, Foerster and Drysdale. Tocchet says he'll give the unit time.

broadstreethockey.com
MIN
Lineup

Shabanov skating with Kaprizov; Coleman with Eriksson Ek and Boldy

New signing Maxim Shabanov is building chemistry on Kirill Kaprizov's line, and Hynes says he's improving daily. Newcomer Blake Coleman is on a line with Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy. The penalty kill was a camp focus.

Defenseman Maxence Guenette waived

Boston put the 25-year-old depth defenseman on waivers on Sept. 23. It was one of the first cuts before the final preseason games.

Waivers

CBJ cut camp to 34; Pheonix Copley waived, two placed on injured non-roster

Goalie Pheonix Copley and forwards James Malatesta and Owen Sillinger were waived to be sent to AHL Cleveland. Six others, including Jordan Dumais and Luca Pinelli, were loaned to Cleveland, and Riley Bezeau and Caleb MacDonald were placed on injured non-roster.

Waivers

Flyers waive six, including Grundstrom and Aston-Reese

Philadelphia waived forwards Zach Aston-Reese, Nolan Foote, Danila Klimovich and Carl Grundstrom and defenseman Cam Dineen, and sent others to Lehigh Valley. Grundstrom had been practicing on the projected fourth line.

Waivers

Canucks waive Fix-Wolansky, Clayton and Schuldt; Mancini looks set as the 7th defenseman

Vancouver cut camp to 31 players. Trey Fix-Wolansky, Cole Clayton and Jimmy Schuldt were waived for AHL assignment. Keeping Victor Mancini while cutting Kirill Kudryavtsev suggests Mancini has won the 7th defense spot.

Wild give GM Bill Guerin a multiyear extension

Luke Hughes starts camp healthy, reunited with Brett Pesce

Report: Blues shopping surplus depth forwards

Friedman says St. Louis has let teams know it has extra depth veterans to move. Named candidates include Berggren, Finley, Walker, Dube and Sundqvist, plus pricier Toropchenko ($2.5M) and Suter ($4.125M).

News

Bettman: no rush on expansion; clarity expected by December

After the Sept. 22 Board of Governors meeting, Bettman said no expansion decisions were made. The league is studying interest from the Friedkin family (Houston/Austin) and groups in Atlanta and Phoenix. Three-quarters of the governors must approve.

NYR 2–0 DET

New York Rangers21 shots
2
FinalLittle Caesars Arena
Detroit Red Wings22 shots
0
123TSOG
NYR101221

Puckline's report

Detroit's home opener had everything a long-suffering fan base could want: booing their own former captain before puck drop, then 60 minutes of not scoring. Dylan Garand, the Rangers' fill-in on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped all 22 shots for the shutout, which is what happens when the other team's shots arrive gift-wrapped. Sean Durzi scored on the power play 5:12 in and later fought Marco Kasper, a full night's work before the third period. Eeli Tolvanen hit the empty net with 1:16 left. John Gibson made 19 saves on 20 and got nothing for it but a sympathetic slap on the pads. New York is 2-1 and has won two straight. Detroit is 0-1, has no goals, no captain and a 10-season playoff drought, and the season is one game old.

By Puckline Prince

5
FinalLenovo Center

2
123TSOG

Puckline's report

The Capitals walked into the champs' building and had it 3-0 before the first intermission, the hockey version of showing up to a party and eating the cake. Alex Tuch scored twice in his Washington debut, and rookie defenseman Cole Hutson scored in his NHL debut, which beats the usual first-game souvenir of a puck and a nervous smile. Ovechkin got an assist on the opening goal, Jakob Chychrun had a power-play goal and an assist, and Dylan Strome and Pierre-Luc Dubois had two helpers each. Sebastian Aho finally got Carolina a power-play goal in the second, and Ryan Leonard answered eight seconds later, which is just rude. Logan Thompson made 31 saves on 33; Brandon Bussi let in five on 27. The Hurricanes outshot Washington and lost by three: 0-1-1, one goal in two home games, and the banner is already the best thing they've put up this season.

Boston Bruins30 shots
4

Winnipeg Jets33 shots

Puckline's report

Winnipeg's home opener was a lovely evening right up until the last 1:38. The Jets led 3-2 after Mario Ferraro scored with eight seconds left in the second, Kyle Connor had a power-play goal, an assist and nine shots, and the Canada Life Centre was ready to go home happy. Then Boston pulled Jeremy Swayman, and Elias Lindholm tied it 6-on-5 at 18:22 of the third. JJ Peterka, two games into his Bruins career, won it 3:21 into overtime for his second goal. David Pastrnak and Nikita Zadorov set up two goals each, Hampus Lindholm and James Hagens also scored, and Mark Kastelic and Tyrel Bauer dropped the gloves early. Swayman stopped 30 of 33, Stuart Skinner 26 of 30. Boston is 2-0. Winnipeg got a point for its trouble, and a reminder that its former Vezina winner is still suspended for skipping camp and still waiting on a trade. Nothing says 'new season' like the old goalie problem.

Puckline's report

Dallas spent the summer near the top of everybody's rankings and opened its season by getting shut out at home. Mason McTavish, playing his first game as a Blue, scored 94 seconds in, and the Stars spent the next 58 minutes looking for a reply. Dalibor Dvorsky made it 2-0 in the second, then St. Louis hit the empty net twice in 15 seconds, Jimmy Snuggerud and Pius Suter, with Joel Hofer picking up an assist on the second one. Hofer stopped all 25 shots for the shutout and outscored the entire Dallas roster in points. Jake Oettinger made 20 saves on 22 and deserved a better band in front of him. Jake Neighbours and Arttu Hyry fought in the second, the closest Dallas came to winning a battle all night. A 112-point team with Jason Robertson locked up, and the first goal of their season will have to wait for Nashville.

Puckline's report

Anaheim's season opener in Vegas went great for about 45 minutes and then got very Vegas. Beckett Sennecke scored with eight seconds left in the first, Alex Killorn and Jeff Malott scored 55 seconds apart early in the second, and Leo Carlsson, the guy the Ducks paid to keep away from Philadelphia, made it 4-0 at 7:03. The Golden Knights trailed by four on home ice to a team that just lost half its summer roster, and the Strip briefly considered a dinner show. Then Shea Theodore, Tomas Hertl on the power play and Braeden Bowman with 2:50 left made it 4-3, and Jack Eichel had two assists in the rally. Lukas Dostal held on with 27 saves on 30. Carter Hart let in four on 20. Vegas played the last 20 minutes like Cup finalists and the first 40 like the house was comping the other team.

CHI @ BUF · 7:00 PM ET

Chicago BlackhawksCHI0-2-0 · 0 PTS
@7:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · KeyBank Center
Buffalo SabresBUF0-1-0 · 0 PTS

Puckline preview

Buffalo's home opener comes with a new problem: the Sabres are a playoff team now, so people expect things. Last spring they ended the NHL's record 14-year playoff drought and won a round before Montreal beat them in seven. Then they opened this season with a 6-3 loss in Columbus, going 0-for-5 on the power play, including a full two minutes of 5-on-3. Olen Zellweger is cleared from concussion protocol and expected to make his Sabres debut, and Lindy Ruff hadn't picked between Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and Colten Ellis as of Friday.

Chicago wraps up three road games in five nights having been outscored 11-2, with 15 shots in Thursday's 6-0 loss in Utah. Connor Bedard is out until November at the earliest after shoulder surgery, so it's Patrick Kane, 37, and a lot of kids. Spencer Knight is likely back in net, though Chicago hadn't confirmed it. Bowen Byram faces the Sabres for the first time since the trade that sent him to Chicago, and he's off the top pair after it was outshot 12-1 early in Utah. Buffalo won both meetings last season, 9-3 and 5-1, with Tage Thompson scoring twice in the last one. Two games is a tiny sample, but so far the Hawks' offense is a rumor.

By Puckline Prince

OTT @ TOR · 7:00 PM ET

Ottawa SenatorsOTT0-0-0 · Opening night
@7:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Scotiabank Arena
Toronto Maple LeafsTOR1-1-0 · 2 PTS

Puckline preview

The Battle of Ontario opens Ottawa's season, and the Senators have owned it lately: three wins in four meetings last season, the last three in a row, ending with a 3-1 win on April 15 built on power-play goals from Drake Batherson and Warren Foegele. Ottawa made the playoffs at 99 points before Carolina swept it; Toronto finished with 78 points and a minus-46, which is a lot of minus for a team with Auston Matthews. Since then Brady Tkachuk was traded to Florida, Thomas Chabot became captain, the Leafs' social team joked about mailing Tkachuk's podcast mic to Florida, and Toronto hired Ottawa legend Daniel Alfredsson onto its coaching staff. The pettiness is in midseason form.

Toronto is 1-1 under new coach Jim Hiller, with Kirill Marchenko on Matthews' wing after the Matthew Knies trade. Sergei Bobrovsky is projected in goal; he stopped 21 of 24 in a 3-2 loss to Montreal before Anthony Stolarz beat the Islanders. Linus Ullmark is expected for Ottawa, Foegele is off IR and projected on the top line, and Jake Sanderson skated Friday and could play. Friedman says the Leafs tried to flip Miles Wood the day they got him, so the roster is still under construction. Two games is no sample, but the Leafs' power play is 1-for-7.

By Puckline Prince

WSH @ TBL · 7:00 PM ET

Washington CapitalsWSH1-0-0 · 2 PTS
@7:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Benchmark International Arena
Tampa Bay LightningTBL0-1-0 · 0 PTS

Puckline preview

Tampa Bay's home opener comes with a scolding still ringing. After Thursday's 5-1 loss to the Rangers, Jon Cooper said it was almost like the game was an inconvenience to play, like it got in the way of summer. The Lightning went 0-for-7 on the power play and gave up an empty-netter to Igor Shesterkin, a goalie, which is a sentence no franchise wants in its media guide. Their last meaningful game before that was a Game 7 loss to Montreal in the first round. Now John Carlson, who played 18 seasons in Washington before a March trade to Anaheim and a July 1 signing in Tampa, faces the Caps for the first time.

Washington is on the second night of a back-to-back after beating the champs 5-2 in Raleigh: Alex Tuch scored twice in his Caps debut, rookie Cole Hutson scored in his NHL debut, and Logan Thompson made 31 saves. The Caps said before the season that Charlie Lindgren gets this one. Alex Ovechkin had an assist Friday and still sits at 929 career goals, the most ever. Last season Tampa took two of three, the last a 5-3 win in Washington with two goals and two assists from Brandon Hagel and a Tom Wilson fight with Curtis Douglas. One game each is no sample, but the Bolts' power play is still looking for its first.

By Puckline Prince

CAR @ PHI · 7:00 PM ET

Carolina HurricanesCAR0-1-1 · 1 PTS
@7:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Xfinity Mobile Arena
Philadelphia FlyersPHI0-1-1 · 1 PTS

Puckline preview

Carolina and Philadelphia can't settle anything in 60 minutes. All four regular-season meetings last year went past regulation, three to shootouts, and the last one, April 13 in Philly, took seven rounds before Tyson Foerster won it; Alexander Nikishin was stopped in the eighth, and he's now an unsigned holdout, so that may stand as his last shootout for the Canes. In May the Hurricanes swept the Flyers in the second round on the way to the Cup.

Both teams are 0-1-1 and each has two goals. Carolina is on the second night of a back-to-back after a 5-2 home loss to Washington that Logan Stankoven called lethargic and unacceptable. The champs' power play is 1-for-12, Seth Jarvis is still out after shoulder surgery, Pyotr Kochetkov is expected to make his season debut, and Jordan Martinook plays his 800th NHL game. The Flyers opened with a 7-0 home loss to Pittsburgh, then got outshot 44-25 in an overtime loss in New Jersey, where Rick Tocchet benched rookies Porter Martone and Alex Bump for most of the third. Dan Vladar is the likely starter, though Joseph Woll made 41 saves in that one. Two games is nothing, but these offenses have combined for four goals in four games, so bring a shootout snack.

By Puckline Prince

MTL @ PIT · 7:00 PM ET

Montreal CanadiensMTL1-0-0 · 2 PTS
@7:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · PPG Paints Arena
Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT1-0-0 · 2 PTS

Puckline preview

Pittsburgh's home opener features the best goal differential in the league, on a sample of one game. The Penguins won 7-0 in Philadelphia, the largest season-opening road shutout in NHL history: Nick Robertson scored twice, Filip Hallander had a goal and two assists, and Arturs Silovs stopped all 19 shots. Silovs is the likely starter again. Andrei Kuzmenko is back with the team and expected to make his Penguins debut, Blake Lizotte is expected out, and Ben Kindel's status was still unsettled Friday. Sidney Crosby is in his 22nd season, which is roughly how long Pittsburgh has been told its window is closing.

Montreal hasn't played since Tuesday's 3-2 win in Toronto, where Alexandre Carrier's unassisted goal held up and Jakub Dobes made 26 saves. The Habs hadn't named a goalie as of Friday. Last spring Montreal went to the conference final, through Tampa Bay and Buffalo in seven games each; Pittsburgh lost in six to Philadelphia in the first round, and judging by Wednesday it's still taking that out on the Flyers. Chris Kreider skates on the top line with Nick Suzuki and Cole Caufield, and Oliver Kapanen looks set to sit again. Montreal took two of three last season, but the last meeting went to Pittsburgh in a shootout, with Rickard Rakell scoring the winner.

By Puckline Prince

UTA @ CBJ · 7:00 PM ET

Utah MammothUTA1-0-0 · 2 PTS
@7:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Nationwide Arena
Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ1-0-0 · 2 PTS

Puckline preview

Two 1-0 teams that both scored six on Thursday, which tells you plenty about Thursday and almost nothing else. Columbus is one game into the Matthew Knies era: the Blue Jackets sent Kirill Marchenko to Toronto for him on Sept. 28, and Knies answered with two goals and an assist in a 6-3 win over Buffalo. Adam Fantilli, a week after signing for six years and $82.5 million, scored too. The worry is the back end: Ivan Provorov, Dante Fabbro and Damon Severson are all out, so Carson Soucy, who was on a camp tryout until this week, is playing real minutes. Jet Greaves is expected back in goal.

Utah blanked Chicago 6-0, with Dylan Guenther scoring twice on the power play and Karel Vejmelka needing all of 15 saves, less a shutout than a light shift at the office. He's expected to start again, though the Mammoth are in New York tomorrow. These two like overtime: Dmitri Voronkov won it on a power play in Salt Lake City in January, and Logan Cooley answered at Nationwide on March 7, his second goal of a 5-4 win after Columbus had erased a two-goal third-period lead. One game each, so that perfect Utah penalty kill is a sample, not a personality.

By Puckline Prince

SEA @ EDM · 7:00 PM ET

Seattle KrakenSEA1-0-0 · 2 PTS
@7:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Rogers Place
Edmonton OilersEDM1-0-1 · 3 PTS

Puckline preview

The Oilers have played two games and allowed 13 goals, which is a lot even for a team that also scored 14. Opening night was a 6-5 overtime loss to Vancouver with Tristan Jarry giving up six on 23 shots; the rematch was a 9-7 win in Vancouver with Devon Levi giving up seven on 22, and Levi is expected to start again tonight. Connor McDavid had five points in that one, and Evan Bouchard has eight through two games. Edmonton is doing it without Zach Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, and Frederik Andersen isn't expected back until December. Defense in Edmonton remains a rumor.

Seattle opened with a 6-1 win in Calgary behind Joey Daccord's 24 saves, but the Kraken's preview has Philipp Grubauer starting here, with Daccord lined up for Monday's home opener. Vince Dunn and Jared McCann have three points apiece, and Matty Beniers is projected to center the top line. The subplot: Elliotte Friedman reported last week that the Oilers asked Seattle about Shane Wright, whose agent says he's fully committed to the Kraken. Wright gets to show the shoppers what they can't have. Last time here, March 31, Connor Ingram stopped all 27 shots in a 3-0 Oilers win and McDavid scored. One and two games played: tiny samples, big goal totals.

NJD @ NYI · 7:30 PM ET

New Jersey DevilsNJD1-0-0 · 2 PTS
@7:30 PM ETSat Oct 3 · UBS Arena
New York IslandersNYI0-1-0 · 0 PTS

Puckline preview

It's the Islanders' home opener, and the Devils walk back into the building where they lost 9-0 in January. That was the night Anthony Duclair had a natural hat trick and five points and Ilya Sorokin stopped all 44 shots for a franchise-record 26th career shutout. New York swept all four meetings last season, the last a 3-1 win on Feb. 5, and Sorokin starts again tonight. The Islanders lost their opener 2-1 in Toronto, and Peter DeBoer spent Friday reshuffling lines and asking for more 5-on-5 scoring: Emil Heineman stays with Bo Horvat and Kyle Palmieri, and rookie Victor Eklund moves in with Cal Ritchie and Brayden Schenn. Mathew Barzal is out with a knee injury. Matthew Schaefer, 19, is now the youngest alternate captain in team history.

New Jersey beat Philadelphia 3-2 in overtime and outshot the Flyers 44-25, which looks dominant until you check the score. Jake Allen is projected in goal. The blue line is short: Johnathan Kovacevic sits out the weekend and Seamus Casey is out 8-10 weeks. Both power plays went 0-for-4 in their openers, so somebody's drought ends tonight, or nobody's does. One game each: small samples, long grudge.

By Puckline Prince

DAL @ NSH · 8:00 PM ET

Dallas StarsDAL0-1-0 · 0 PTS
@8:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Bridgestone Arena
Nashville PredatorsNSH0-1-0 · 0 PTS

Puckline preview

Dallas has to turn around and play the night after getting shut out 4-0 at home by St. Louis. Joel Hofer stopped all 25 shots, the Blues added two empty-netters 15 seconds apart late, and the Stars went 0-for-4 on the power play, which is a rough look for a top unit with Mikko Rantanen, Jason Robertson and Wyatt Johnston on it. Casey DeSmith, freshly extended at two years and $5 million, is expected to start the back half of the back-to-back. Matt Duchene is on LTIR and can't play before Oct. 25.

Nashville lost its opener 3-1 at home to Minnesota and was outshot 30-20. Ryan Ufko got sent to Milwaukee after one game, Andrew Brunette is reshuffling his defense pairs and says he wants someone to grab a job, and Jeff Marek says the Predators have been looking at Montreal's spare defensemen. Ryan O'Reilly is in a contract year, and Friedman says executives call that an underreported story. Juuse Saros is expected in goal. The Stars won all three meetings last season, each by one goal, the last a 3-2 overtime comeback on Feb. 28 finished by Robertson off a Miro Heiskanen feed. One game each, so the panic is premature, but Nashville fans have had plenty of practice.

BOS @ MIN · 8:00 PM ET

Boston BruinsBOS2-0-0 · 4 PTS
@8:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Grand Casino Arena
Minnesota WildMIN1-0-0 · 2 PTS

Puckline preview

Boston is 2-0 and neither win was boring. Jeremy Swayman shut out the Rangers in the opener, then Friday in Winnipeg the Bruins trailed late until Elias Lindholm tied it with the goalie pulled and JJ Peterka won it 3:21 into overtime. James Hagens, 19, scored his first NHL goal and David Pastrnak had two assists. Two games is a tiny sample, but they're doing it without Charlie McAvoy, whose suspension runs until Oct. 13. It's the second night of a back-to-back, so Michael DiPietro is reported to get the net, his first NHL start since January 2022. Pavel Zacha plays on in a contract year; Chris Johnston says the sides are struggling to agree on a number.

Minnesota's home opener follows a 3-1 win in Nashville, with Jesper Wallstedt stopping 19 of 20 while Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber sit on IR. Quinn Hughes is the other contract story: LeBrun says he just hasn't told his camp to close an extension. Last March in Boston, Zacha and Lindholm scored twice each in a 6-3 Bruins win that cost the Wild a chance to clinch a playoff spot. The Wild got in anyway, won their first series since 2015, then blew a 3-0 lead in the game that ended their season against Colorado. Very on brand.

By Puckline Prince

STL @ COL · 9:00 PM ET

St Louis BluesSTL1-0-0 · 2 PTS
@9:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Ball Arena
Colorado AvalancheCOL1-0-0 · 2 PTS

Puckline preview

St. Louis opened Friday with a 4-0 win in Dallas: Joel Hofer stopped all 25 shots, Mason McTavish scored 94 seconds in, and the Blues added two empty-netters 15 seconds apart. It wasn't all clean. Brandon Carlo was ejected in his Blues debut with a kneeing major on Roope Hintz (Hintz returned), and we haven't seen word of further discipline. Alexey Toropchenko left hurt and Jim Montgomery called it more than day-to-day. It's the second night of a back-to-back, and NHL.com's Lou Korac reported Jordan Binnington gets this one. Off the ice, the Blues are reported to be the one real suitor for Carolina's unsigned Alexander Nikishin.

Colorado opened with an 8-4 win over Los Angeles, going 4-for-5 on the power play, with rookie T.J. Hughes debuting on the top unit and Brock Nelson getting three points. One game each, so read nothing into it yet. Last season the Avs won the Presidents' Trophy, then got swept by Vegas in the conference final, which is like acing every quiz and skipping the exam. Jared Bednar got an extension through 2030-31 anyway. Last April these two met twice in three days: Robert Thomas had a hat trick in a 3-2 Blues win in Denver, then Colorado took the rematch 3-1 in St. Louis.

CGY @ VAN · 10:00 PM ET

Calgary FlamesCGY0-1-0 · 0 PTS
@10:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · Rogers Arena
Vancouver CanucksVAN1-1-0 · 2 PTS

Puckline preview

Vancouver has scored 13 goals and allowed 14 in two games, which is less a hockey team than a pickup game with a Zamboni. Paul Cotter scored shorthanded and won it in overtime in his Canucks debut Tuesday in Edmonton; two nights later the Oilers put up nine in Vancouver's home opener and Kevin Lankinen was pulled after eight goals on 20 shots. Tiny sample, but the defense has some explaining to do. Manny Malhotra shuffled all four lines Friday, moving Marco Rossi to wing with Elias Pettersson, and Jake DeBrusk skated as the extra and said he isn't 100 percent, so he could sit (reported). Thatcher Demko is aiming to be back from hip surgery before Christmas; until then it's Lankinen and Leevi Merilainen, who are expected to split this weekend.

Calgary's last home opener at the Saddledome was a 6-1 loss to Seattle, with Ryan Strome scoring the only goal. Devin Cooley is reported to be in line for a start tonight or Sunday in Seattle, and Jonathan Huberdeau is on IR. Last time these two met, March 28 in Calgary, seven different Flames scored in a 7-3 win and Vancouver used two goalies. Pettersson has 34 points in 32 career games against Calgary, so somebody here enjoys this rivalry.

By Puckline Prince

LAK @ SJS · 10:00 PM ET

Los Angeles KingsLAK0-1-0 · 0 PTS
@10:00 PM ETSat Oct 3 · SAP Center at San Jose
San Jose SharksSJS1-0-0 · 2 PTS

Puckline preview

The Kings' new era started in Denver on Wednesday and lasted about as long as it took Colorado to score eight. It was Peter Laviolette's first game behind the bench and LA's first season opener since Anze Kopitar retired, and the Avs went 4-for-5 on the power play while Darcy Kuemper allowed eight on 29 shots. One game is a tiny sample, but the penalty kill killed exactly one penalty. LA hasn't said whether Kuemper goes again or Anton Forsberg gets the start, and Kevin Fiala is still on IR. Colorado also swept the Kings in the first round last spring, so this was more of a reunion than a fluke.

San Jose opened with a 4-3 overtime win over Florida: Will Smith scored twice, Mason Marchment scored in his Sharks debut, Luca Cagnoni won it, and Macklin Celebrini, 20 and the youngest captain in team history, had three assists. Yaroslav Askarov is expected in net; he's 3-1-0 career against LA. The Sharks won two of three meetings last season, the last one Jan. 7 in Los Angeles, when Celebrini had a goal and two assists and set up William Eklund's overtime winner. Smith's extension still isn't done, and both he and GM Mike Grier say they aren't worried.

By Puckline Prince
